In the US, you can't sue for this either, unless you can demonstrate that you had to go to the hospital and had medical bills because of some infection.

Part of the US's sue-happy culture is due to our pay-it-yourself medical system. If someone sends you to the hospital, it both harms you and costs you money. Harm can't be calculated easily, but medical costs are easy to document, so lawsuits exist to recoup those costs from the person responsible. In a socialized medical system, all those costs are covered, so there isn't really anything to sue over other than personal claims that are harder to justify.

And remember a trip to the hospital here can be hundreds of thousands of dollars. Even people who don't want to sue may have no choice. Medical bankruptcy is pretty common. Insurance will still leave you with thousands of dollars of bills after they pay.
